title: ‘Political activities like dharna, satyagraha have no place in democracy’: Kerala High Court

ai.summary: Kerala High Court ruled that political activities like dharna and hunger strikes have no place in constitutional democracy, citing a 2017 judgement that students engaging in such activities can be expelled from academic institutions.

facts.claim: Kerala High Court said political activities like dharna, hunger strikes, and other practices like satyagraha have no place in a constitutional democracy
facts.quote: ‘Political activities like dharna, hunger strikes, and other practices like satyagraha have no place in a constitutional democracy, much less in academic institutions,’

facts.claim: The court cited a 2017 judgement by another bench
facts.quote: the Kerala High Court said on Tuesday, November 3, citing a 2017 judgement by another bench.

facts.claim: The 2017 judgement stated that students engaging in political activities are liable to be expelled or rusticated
facts.quote: In its November 3 order, the bench quoted the 2017 judgement in Dr Antony Thomas v VM Muhammed Rafique and others to say that students engaging in political activities are liable to be expelled or rusticated.

facts.claim: The 2017 judgement quoted Dr BR Ambedkar on constitutional methods
facts.quote: The 2017 judgement had quoted Dr BR Ambedkar to say, ‘If we wish to maintain democracy not merely in form, but also in fact, what must we do? … It means we must abandon the bloody methods of revolution. It means that we must abandon the method of civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha.'

ai.background_note: Kerala High Court ruled that political activities like dharna and hunger strikes have no place in constitutional democracy, citing a 2017 judgement that students engaging in such activities can be expelled from academic institutions.
